title: HIFI-Barcode SOP – Assembling COI barcodes using high-throughput sequencing
author: Shanlin Liu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k9icz4e
materials: 3.1 PCR reaction mixture Consumables & Equipment for PCR amplification 1.10X PCR Buffer for exTaq Store at –20°C. 2.10mM dNTP mix. Store at –20°C 3.molecular grade ddH2O 4.exTaq store at -20°C 5.Microplate(Eppendorf® plates) 6.Cap strips or sealing film 7.Eppendorf 5830R high speed centrifuge 8.primer sets. Ninety-six pairs of different tags were added to both ends of a common COI barcode primer set (LCO1490 and HCO2198) with each tag containing 5 bps allowing for ≥ 2 bp differences from each other. PCR reagents per 25 μl reaction: General recommendations The use of filter tips is recommended for all PCR reagents to avoid contamination. Clean the bench top with alcohol before setting up reactions. Always use a sterile tip when removing exTaq polymerase and the other reagents from their tubes. Keep DNA templates (i.e. other PCR products) away from the PCR reagents while you are setting up the reaction mixes. Add DNA after all of the reagents have been returned to the freezer. Always include a sample without template as a negative control to check for contamination of the reagents. Include a positive control (a DNA sample that has amplified in the past) as well to test the effectiveness of the PCR reagents. 3.2 PCR thermocycle program The amplification program includes a thermocycling profile of : 94°C for 1 min; 5 cycles of 94°C for 30 sec, 45°C for 40 sec, and an extension at 72°C for 1 min; followed by 35 cycles of 94°C for 30 sec, 51°C for 40 sec, and 72°C for 1 min; with a final extension at 72°C for 10 min, and finally holding at 12°C. 3.3 PCR product check All amplicons could be visualized on a 1.2% 96 Agarose E-gel (Biowest Agarose). 10X PCR buffer Takara Bio Inc. 10mM dNTP mix Takara Bio Inc. exTaq Takara Bio Inc. 00:58:40, 3.2

steps.title: Pool PCR products for Illumina
steps.instruction: Take all PCR products from each 96‑well plate and pool 1 µL of each sample, creating two pools of 96 µL each.

steps.title: Fragment amplicons and prepare library
steps.instruction: Fragment the pooled amplicons to generate a library with an insert size of 250 bp and set the sequencing strategy to 150 bp paired‑end (150 PE).

steps.title: Pool PCR products for PacBio
steps.instruction: (Optional) Take all PCR products from each plate and pool 1 µL per sample, producing two 96 µL mixtures for PacBio sequencing.

steps.title: Sequence Illumina library
steps.instruction: Load the Illumina library onto a HiSeq or BGIseq500 instrument and run a 150 PE run.

steps.title: Sequence PacBio library
steps.instruction: (Optional) Load the PacBio library onto a PacBio RS II instrument and perform sequencing.
